name: Directly From My Heart To You

podcast.body: A version of this song was recorded during Richard's last session for Peacock Records, handled by Johnny Otis, but it remained unreleased at the time. He later recorded a decent version of it during his first Specialty Records session. "They also caught a decent version of Directly From My Heart To You, the song which Richard had previously recorded with Johnny Otis."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.body: This R&B ballad is noted as typifying a genre of R&B ballads that influenced James Brown's "Please Please Please." It also owed more than a little to Fay Adams' "Shake a Hand." "This song fits neatly into a particular genre of R&B Ballad, typified by Flow Example Richards directly from my heart to you."
